newcontributor_statements.body:
> Done, switched both to @jit. Also added a test for the branching case from your example, where the second write is behind a branch that never runs and the structural check still rejects it.

Many thanks, I've approved the changes. Congrats on your first contribution to Numba. 🎉

reviews.author: esc
reviews.body:
In general `@jit` is to be preferred over `@njit`. The object mode fallback was removed:

https://numba.readthedocs.io/en/stable/release/0.59.0-notes.html#object-mode-fall-back-support-has-been-removed 

Also, it may be worth adding a check for the branching case, mentioned in the docs:

```
In [2]: @jit
   ...: def f(cond):
   ...:     x = 0
   ...:     def bar():
   ...:         nonlocal x
   ...:         x = 1
   ...:         if cond:
   ...:             x = 2
   ...:     bar()
   ...:     return x
   ...:
   ...: try:
   ...:     f(False)
   ...: except Exception as e:
   ...:     print(type(e).__name__, e)
   ...:
UnsupportedError Failed in nopython mode pipeline (step: inline calls to locally defined closures)
Reassigning the nonlocal variable 'x' inside an inlined closure is unsupported. Assign it once instead.

File "<ipython-input-2-2d399f210c6e>", line 9:
    def bar():
        <source elided>
            x = 2
    bar()
    ^

During: Pass inline_closure_likes
```
